Compliance and Enforcement Priorities webinar

We’ve refreshed our Enforcement and Compliance Priorities for 2025/26. Since announcing them in December, we’ve taken strong action to protect Kiwi consumers, including:
• Criminal charges against HelloFresh
• $16.9m in refunds from Alpine Energy
• NZ’s first criminal cartel conviction
• Ongoing proceedings against Winstone Wallboards

We unpack these cases and more in our latest webinar.

Reporting a concern to the Commerce Commission

Report your concern on our website: https://comcom.govt.nz/report-a-concern

Kordia Chats - Brent La Franchie

Join us as we celebrate 60 years of Kordia’s iconic towers — Waiatarua, Kaukau, Wharite, and Sugarloaf. Brent shares how these towers shaped nationwide broadcasting, their evolving role today, and how Kordia’s expert team continues to support critical infrastructure across NZ and beyond.

Kordia Chats - Andy Powell

Andy reflects on 60 years of Kordia’s iconic towers, sharing his early days working at Wharite and what made the job special. He also talks about how the network has evolved and the crucial work the team does today to keep our critical communications infrastructure running strong.

Celebrating Taumarunui's Rail Heritage - Saturday 23 August 2025

Around 300 people gathered in Taumarunui on Saturday 23 August to celebrate the township’s rich rail heritage.

A highlight of the day was a journey in historic carriages pulled by a steam locomotive from Glenbrook Vintage Railway. The trip from Taumarunui to Ongarue offered passengers stunning views of the Ruapehu–King Country landscape as the train followed the Ongarue River.

In Ongarue, passengers visited the memorial to the 1923 Ongarue rail disaster. On 6 July that year, an overnight express struck a landslip, claiming 17 lives and injuring 28 of the 200 people on board. It was the first major rail tragedy in New Zealand’s history.

The event blended enjoyment of the region’s rail past with a moment of reflection, honouring both the joy and the challenges of the railway’s legacy.

If your planning a trip to Ruapehu consider travelling on the Northern Explorer which stops in Taumarunui, Waimarino-National Park and Ohakune. 
See: visitruapehu.com or greatjourneysnz.com

Achieving equitable wellbeing outcomes for tāngata whaiora: what we know, what needs to change

Te Hiringa Mahara hosted a webinar outlining findings from our 2025 Assessment of wellbeing for people who interact with mental health and addiction services.

The assessment released on 25 June is our first assessment comparing the status of wellbeing for people who interact with mental health and addiction services when compared compared to the rest of the population. It found that people who interact with mental health and addiction services experience systemic disadvantage in access to the determinants of mental health and wellbeing. This includes: lower household income; fewer social connections; and poorer individual, family and whānau wellbeing.

The panel discussed findings from the assessment, approaches to improving wellbeing for whānau Māori, and lived experience perspectives of social determinants.

Our speakers were:

Alex El Amanni, Addiction Practitioner and Counsellor, Te Hiringa Mahara board member
Laura Ross, Kaitohu Mātaamua o te Pūnaha Toiora | Principal Advisor Wellbeing System, Te Hiringa Mahara
Professor Te Kani Kingi, Executive Director of Research and Innovation at Te Whare Wānanga o Awanuiārangi
The session will be hosted by Dr Ella Cullen, Kaiwhakahaere Pūnaha Toiora Arataki | Director of Wellbeing System Leadership, Te Hiringa Mahara.

Have your say on the new draft disability strategy (closing 28 September)

Whaikaha is pleased to open consultation on New Zealand’s draft disability strategy. In this video, Whaikaha CEO Paula Tesoriero shares the news alongside an NZSL interpeter.

Consultation closes on Sunday 28 September. Please make sure you have your say. 

The draft strategy is important because it will guide the Government’s work for the next 5 years, and it's now time to hear what you think of it. 

To find out more and give your thoughts, visit www.whaikaha.govt.nz/disability-strategy

Full script:

Tēnā koutou katoa, Talofa Lava, Mālō a leilei, Bula vinaka, warm Pacific greetings.     

My name is Paula, I’m the chief executive of the Ministry of Disabled People - Whaikaha.  

My sign name is this (demonstrates move) which is two fists moving in a forward direction like a bicycle. 

Today, Whaikaha is pleased to be opening consultation on New Zealand’s draft disability strategy. 

Our current disability strategy will end next year.  The draft strategy is important because it will guide the Government’s work for the next five years and it's now time to hear what you think of it.
 
We’ve worked with members of the disability community – as well as Government and sector representatives – to create the draft.  We are grateful for the time and expertise people have provided, alongside a willingness to collaborate.  

The draft strategy includes a new vision and new principles. There are also goals and actions in areas that are important to disabled people such as employment, health, housing, education and justice.  

There’re lots of ways to provide feedback such as filling out our online feedback form, or by registering to attend an online or in-person meeting. 

You can details and copies of the strategy, in alternate formats, on our website at www.whaikaha.govt.nz/disability-strategy 

Consultation closes on Sunday 28 September. Make sure you have your say. 

Let’s make New Zealand a place where disabled people thrive.
